clue.text: Penchant for endless misbelief, bar the odd …

indicators.note: endless asks for the last letter of the word for to be cut off

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: barring the odd letters of misbelief leaves only its even-placed ones

explanation.surface: Someone with a taste for disbelief is halted mid-thought, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next in the surface only. 'endless' trims FOR to FO; 'bar the odd' keeps the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of misbelief, I, B, L, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A foible is a small personal weakness or quirk, close to a penchant or fondness for something.

clue.text: … doubt as blue whale's tail fin exploded

indicators.note: something exploded is blown to bits, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Doubt arises when a blue whale's fin is blown apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' shuffles BLUE, E (the tail of whale's) and FIN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbelief is a lack of faith or conviction, which amounts to doubt.

clue.text: Nine lives heartlessly destroyed by serial killer

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle of lives is removed, leaving its two ends

explanation.surface: A cat's nine lives are wiped out by a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves LS from lives; 'destroyed' rearranges NINE plus LS. Dennis Nilsen was a British serial killer of the late 1970s and early 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis Nilsen is the name of a notorious British murderer convicted of multiple killings in 1983.

clue.text: Italian birds circling on rising

indicators.note: circling means the birds go round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: geese are birds

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word on is read upwards, back to front

explanation.surface: Italian birds wheel around while climbing into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads a word upwards; 'circling' has the birds go round it. Genoa is a port city in north-west Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoese describes a person or thing from Genoa, a city in Italy.

clue.text: No time to ask "Why's head visible?"

indicators.note: no time means the letter T, standing for time, is dropped

parts.note: to invite someone is to ask them along

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a certain head has come into sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No time' takes T out of INVITE to leave INVIE; 'head' supplies W from Why's.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in view can be seen, an idiom for being visible.

clue.text: Kierkegaard's choice of leading man in bizarre rite

indicators.note: in places the leading man inside the rearranged letters
bizarre means strange, so the letters of rite are twisted out of order

parts.note: the hero is the leading man of a story or film

explanation.surface: The philosopher chooses a leading man for a strange ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre' signals the anagram of rite and 'in' the insertion. The hyphenated (6-2) count points to the Danish philosopher's famous title rather than a generic choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Either/Or is the title of Søren Kierkegaard's 1843 book about choosing between ways of life.

clue.text: Less appealing aspects of some Ulster teams

parts.note: County Down is one part of the province of Ulster
sides are teams in a game

explanation.surface: Northern Irish teams have their drawbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is one of the six Northern Irish counties in Ulster, so 'some Ulster' is that county.
explanation.definitionFit: Downsides are disadvantages, the less attractive features of something.

clue.text: Bank eschewing limits to reported credit caper

indicators.note: eschewing limits means avoiding the outer letters of Bank, keeping its middle
reported means a word as heard, spelt differently

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A bank's reported credit dealings turn out to be a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eschewing limits' leaves AN from Bank; 'reported' says TICK (credit) is heard as TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or grotesque act, the same as a caper or prank.

clue.text: Recycling is one boss's hobby horse

indicators.note: recycling remakes material into something new, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the possessive adds no letter, leaving boss

explanation.surface: Recycling is the boss's pet subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycling' rearranges IS ONE BOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a fixation, much like a hobby horse that someone keeps returning to.

clue.text: Print short story, however brief

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for a story is cut

parts.note: a lie is a story, a tall tale

indicators.note: brief means the word for however is abbreviated to its informal short form

parts.note: though means however

explanation.surface: A short story gets printed, however brief it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts LIE to LI; 'brief' cuts THOUGH to its informal spelling THO.
explanation.definitionFit: A litho is a print made by lithography, printing from a flat inked surface.

clue.text: See 16
Foreign article starts to seriously infect leg wound

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: starts means the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: An imported substance begins to seriously infect a leg injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes S and I from seriously infect.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is a region of damaged tissue, such as a wound or ulcer.

clue.text: Start striking bit of organ playing?

definitions.meaning: to begin an industrial strike is to down tools
read as a ..., an organ stop doing its job while the instrument plays

explanation.walkthrough: An organ stop is a knob that brings in a set of pipes; the question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop work is to cease labour, which is how a strike by workers begins.

clue.text: Examples of house style in Faber's page-turner

indicators.note: a page-turner here is something that turns letters over, a rearranging signal

parts.note: the publisher's name with its s kept

explanation.surface: Examples of house style appear in a gripping book from the publisher Faber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turner' rearranges FABERS and P; 'page-turner' looks like a gripping novel and 'house style' like a publisher's rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefabs are prefabricated houses, so each is an example of a style of house.

clue.text: Forcefully push through bar, holding a gun?

parts.note: a rail is a bar

indicators.note: holding means the gun encloses the letter a

parts.note: rod is American slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Someone forces their way through a bar while holding a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A inside ROD to make ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad a measure is to rush or force it through without proper discussion.

clue.text: Eg pot with opening for spout

parts.note: pot, cannabis, is an example of what is called blow in slang
a hole is an opening

explanation.surface: A pot with a hole for pouring through.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a teapot; pot is really the drug, and blow is a British slang term for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale's blowhole is also called its spout or spout-hole, through which it breathes out.

clue.text: Her veal's cooked in port

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared and changed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A woman's veal is cooked in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges HER VEAL. Le Havre is a French port on the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major seaport in Normandy, France.

clue.text: Very important learner follows lively name-dropping badinage

indicators.note: follows puts the learner after the rest
lively means the remaining letters are stirred into fresh order
dropping means the letter for name is taken out of badinage

parts.note: L is the learner plate sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A very important learner follows some lively banter full of famous names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name-dropping' looks like showing off famous acquaintances but here removes N; 'lively' gives ABIGDEA from what is left, and 'follows' puts the learner last.
explanation.definitionFit: A big deal is an idiom for something or someone that matters a great deal.

clue.text: Film little boy with bird

parts.note: Wes is a short form of the boy's name Wesley
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A film about a small boy and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a film genre set in the American Old West.

clue.text: Strikes a chord, having screwed this in

indicators.note: screwed means twisted, so the letters of this are turned about

parts.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A remark that strikes a chord, like a screw driven home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screwed' rearranges THIS; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit home is to have a strong effect, an idiom close to striking a chord.

clue.text: Plant that is less wild part of 4's 22 across

indicators.note: wild means the letters run free into a new order

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant that is less wild than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges IE and LESS. The clue also gives the plant a second way: it is hidden across 'Genoese's elixir' (4's 22 across), genoeSES ELIxir.
explanation.definitionFit: Seseli is a genus of flowering plants in the carrot family.

clue.text: Essential solution sees priest kiss taxmen once

parts.note: Eli is the priest of the Old Testament who brought up Samuel
x stands for a kiss at the end of a letter
the IR, Inland Revenue, was the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: A priest kisses former tax inspectors to find a solution.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was merged into HMRC in 2005, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a potion or solution, thought of as the essential remedy or essence.

clue.text: Gradually moving the border

definitions.meaning: a decorative trim round the edge of something

explanation.definitionFit: Edging means inching forward, and also a strip that borders something.

clue.text: Confession by former drug dealer's legendary lover?

parts.note: a confession is spoken in the first person, so the dealer says I
a former dealer's trade is told in the past tense: sold
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A former drug dealer's admission concerns a famous lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The confession reads I SOLD E: the former dealer admits selling ecstasy. Isolde is the Irish princess loved by Tristan.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the heroine of the Tristan legend, one of the great doomed lovers.

clue.text: Like some setters covered in hair, I shave

indicators.note: covered in means the answer is concealed within the next words

explanation.surface: A man covered in hair decides to shave.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters here are dogs: the Irish setter is a red gundog breed, not a crossword compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish setter is a breed of dog, so Irish describes some setters.

clue.text: Film actor's entrance

definitions.meaning: a 1937 Hollywood movie starring Katharine Hepburn
the backstage door at a theatre used by performers

explanation.definitionFit: Stage Door is a 1937 film, and the name for the theatre door that performers use.

clue.text: Fixes tax account?

definitions.meaning: tax sounds like tacks, and an account of tacks would list them as small pins

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: tax heard as tacks, which are a kind of small nail.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail is to fix something in place, and tacks are a form of small pins.

clue.text: Great Italian PA, first and best of its kind

definitions.text: first and best of its kind

parts.note: gran is Italian for great, as in Gran Premio
pa and daddy are both words for father

explanation.surface: A great Italian personal assistant is the best of the bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: PA looks like a personal assistant but is father.
explanation.definitionFit: The granddaddy of something is the original or greatest example of its type.
